title: Tenali Raman and the Alchemist's Sealed Crucible
summary: A cunning alchemist named Siddha Ramanand set up a laboratory in Vijayanagara, claiming he had perfected a secret clay crucible that could turn common river sand into pure silve...
full_text:
A cunning alchemist named Siddha Ramanand set up a laboratory in Vijayanagara, claiming he had perfected a secret clay crucible that could turn common river sand into pure silver.
Before a gathering of wealthy merchants, he put sand into the crucible, sealed it with wax, heated it in a charcoal furnace, and opened it:
Inside were ten bright, solid silver beads!
The merchants were dazzled, offering thousands of gold coins to buy the 'miraculous crucible'.

Tenali Raman attended the demonstration.
He examined the crucible: it was an ordinary earthenware pot coated with dark red clay slip.
Tenali smiled: 'Master Siddha, your alchemy is magnificent!
Let us perform the trial once more before King Krishnadevaraya in the royal palace, using clay and sand provided by the crown!'

The alchemist, unable to refuse without admitting fraud, arrived at the royal audience hall.
Tenali provided an ordinary clay pot, filled it with river sand from the Tungabhadra, and said:
'Now, Master Siddha, seal this pot with your secret wax and heat it in our furnace!'

The alchemist hesitated, sweating profusely:
'Master Tenali, my alchemy works only in my own consecrated laboratory with my own ancestral crucibles!'

Tenali picked up the alchemist’s original 'miraculous crucible' from the table:
'Then let us examine your ancestral vessel!'
Tenali picked up an iron hammer and cleanly cracked the crucible in two!

He held up the broken pieces before the King:
The clay crucible had a **false bottom**!
Between the double layers of clay, the alchemist had concealed ten real silver beads, sealed with wax that melted when heated, allowing the silver to drop into the sand!

The court erupted in outrage!
King Krishnadevaraya ordered the charlatan arrested and his ill-gotten wealth distributed to the cheated merchants.
Tenali laughed:
'Maharaj, those who promise silver from dirt always have their silver hidden in the false bottoms of their own greed!'
The King rewarded Tenali, once again defending public reason against fraud.
moral: Charlatans who claim secret transmutation cannot withstand the bright light of independent testing.
